races.name: Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Dash (Class 2 Handicap)

runners_data.name: Kendall Roy
runners_data.note: Won on this ground and trip in recent form but only 3 wins from 14 similar-going runs in profile — prominent style will face fierce competition for position in a race stacked with handy types; 15 days since last run, good fresh record.|

runners_data.name: Tuco Salamanca
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist stepping back from six to five furlongs; sole recent win came on Standard ground at six, and similar-going record is modest (0W2P from 6), but the contested pace this field will generate is precisely his scenario — jockey Jerry Chau rides aggressively for Ollie Sangster.|

runners_data.name: Fahrenheit Seven
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning after 42 days off; Robert Cowell runners can go well fresh on fast ground and has won at 5f on Good, but recent form shows three consecutive finishes outside the frame and a 0/13 T14 record gives no confidence the yard is flying.|

runners_data.name: Fandom
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner for Richard Hannon with a strong similar-going record (11/13 runs, 1W4P); finished fourth last time but that was over six furlongs — the drop to five furlongs on this fast surface is a genuine question mark over his ability to quicken.|

runners_data.name: Spartan Arrow
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the mount on this prominent-style six-year-old returning after 99 days off — the lengthy break demands caution and his recent form string of 78807 is deeply uninspiring; blinkers worn, Good to Firm suits.|

runners_data.name: All Ways Glamorous
runners_data.note: Back-to-back 5f wins on Good ground is compelling form and the similar-going record of 4W7P from 9 runs is the standout strike-rate in the race — prominent style with proven ability to dominate from the front on fast ground makes this profile interesting whichever shape unfolds.|

runners_data.name: Gaeli
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose only similar-going win came at 1/6 runs in that category — needs the pace to be genuine and rivals to tie up; blinkers worn, 43 days off, and Philip Kirby's T14 record is 0/13, suggesting the yard is not in a hot streak.|

runners_data.name: Gold Star Hero
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has posted three consecutive wins; however, all recent wins came on Standard or softer ground, and his similar-going record is a concerning 0W0P from 9 attempts — the step up to Good to Firm may be his undoing despite his natural ability to dominate early.|

runners_data.name: Bolo Neighs
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's four-year-old has won at 6f on Good ground and shows consistent placed efforts — a natural prominent racer whose instinct is to bowl along in the first two, but the density of pace in this field means he is likely to find himself a length or two further back than ideal, which the STYLE_FIT flag reflects.|

runners_data.name: Cinque Verde
runners_data.note: The other confirmed front-runner, six years old for Tony Carroll; all meaningful form is at six furlongs rather than five, and his similar-going record (2W4P from 8) is respectable but his habit of racing up with the pace at a longer trip may leave him exposed when a horse like Gold Star Hero challenges him for the rail at the shortest trip he's attempted recently.|

runners_data.name: Apollo One
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old handicapper whose form string of 293900 is telling — no wins in 9 recent similar-going attempts (0W2P) and, while a natural prominent type, the redistribution to midfield reflects real-world congestion that will cost him ground; T14 record of 0/5 offers no trainer momentum.|

runners_data.name: Kylian
runners_data.note: Headgear visor suggests a tendency to travel lazily — hold-up profile from Robert Cowell's yard (0/13 T14) who has recorded a win at 5f on Good in recent history; needs the pace to fall apart in front of him and a clear run, neither of which is guaranteed with 12 runners on a straight track.|

races.paceDynamic: Gold Star Hero and Cinque Verde are confirmed front-runners who will clash for the lead from the gates, creating a genuinely contested pace over Ascot's straight five on Good to Firm ground — an honest, high-tempo gallop is the most probable outcome. Five of the twelve runners want a prominent pitch, meaning Kendall Roy, Fahrenheit Seven, Fandom, Spartan Arrow and All Ways Glamorous will all be jostling for the same ground in the first furlong, compressing the field and generating significant traffic and shuffling 2-3 furlongs out. The field holds more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Gold Star Hero and Cinque Verde are best-placed to actually secure their natural positions, while Bolo Neighs and Apollo One, though true prominent racers in their own right, are likely to be squeezed into a midfield berth against their instincts. This contested pace on fast ground over a minimum trip at Ascot classically sets up a race for hold-up horses or those who travel powerfully off a strong clip and finish through beaten rivals — Tuco Salamanca, Gaeli and Kylian are the profile that benefits most from the shape this field will almost certainly produce.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Rewards Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Gold Star Hero and Cinque Verde fight for the lead and empty in the final furlong after setting a fierce pace.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other off and the field strings out, leaving a clear passage for hold-up horses to pick up the pieces late; the Good to Firm surface rewards those with a natural change of gear from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Survivor Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent horses finds a pocket just off the leaders and outlasts the front-runners as they tie up.
scenarios.body: With so much early battle up front, a horse sitting second or third in a perfect pocket — rather than involved in the pace war — has the energy to accelerate when the leaders falter; the flat, straight five at Ascot gives a clean sightline for such a horse to time its run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Leads Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners — most likely Gold Star Hero — breaks cleanly and establishes a clear, uncontested lead by forcing the other to sit off.
scenarios.body: On Good to Firm over five furlongs at Ascot, a single unchallenged pace-setter can occasionally hold on if the early gallop is controlled rather than suicidal; this shape requires the pace battle to resolve quickly in the first fifty yards.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Backmarkers Caught Out Wide
scenarios.trigger: If the field fans wide and traffic fails to materialise, leaving true hold-up horses with too much ground to make up.
scenarios.body: If the race runs to suit a prominent horse that gets an uncontested pitch and the finish is a sprint from two out, genuine hold-up horses are unlikely to close sufficient ground in time; this is the scenario that most disadvantages Tuco Salamanca and Kylian.

watchPoints.text: Gold Star Hero vs Cinque Verde — watch the first 100 yards; if both break fast and lock horns for the lead, the pace will be unsustainably fierce and both will be spent before the final furlong, opening the door for hold-up horses to sweep through.

Prominent congestion between furlongs 3 and 2 — with Kendall Roy, Fahrenheit Seven, Fandom, Spartan Arrow and All Ways Glamorous all hunting the same ground, expect bumping and checking as the field fans out; any runner held up behind this cluster faces a potential traffic nightmare.

Bolo Neighs and Apollo One — both are genuine prominent racers forced into a midfield slot by field congestion; if either gets a trouble-free run and finds their natural stride early, they may outperform their mapped position, but the risk of being caught flat-footed in the first two furlongs is real.

All Ways Glamorous posts the strongest similar-going strike-rate in the field (4W7P from 9 runs) — watch whether Mme Marie Velon positions her prominently enough to exploit it without getting caught in the pace war that Gold Star Hero and Cinque Verde are likely to ignite.

Tuco Salamanca's jockey Jerry Chau — watch for an early decision to drop sharply towards the rear; if Chau commits to that strategy cleanly, Salamanca will be ideally placed to benefit from the contested pace, but at five furlongs there is limited room to make up ground if the run is blocked late.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Stayers (Class 2 Handicap) (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Spirit Mixer
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 8-year-old is the race's engine room, mapping as the lead horse and capable of dictating from the front; has won over 16f on soft and placed on good, though an OR of 94 and top weight means rivals will be watching her every move, and her STYLE_FIT flag suggests she may be stretching her natural role slightly.

runners_data.name: Lavender Hill Mob
runners_data.note: Jamie Melham partners this 5-year-old who is a genuine hold-up horse suited to waiting tactics over extreme trips; won over 21f on soft and placed at 20f on good, though the Good to Firm here is on the quicker side of her best form, and 53 days off the track adds a small fitness question.

runners_data.name: Kilmeaden
runners_data.note: Faye Bramley's 4-year-old is a natural prominent racer who has placed third over 14f on good and fifth over 16f — the step up to 2m is a key unknown for a horse whose form is centred around shorter staying trips; tongue-tie noted and C Y Ho takes the ride for the Rest of the World team.

runners_data.name: Dancing In Paris
runners_data.note: Ian Williams runner who races from hold-up, but recent form reads poorly (15th at Sandown, 12th at Newmarket) and the 2m trip stretches a horse whose best recent effort is a fifth over 12f on good; 15 days between runs suggests connections have kept him fresh but underlying form is hard to enthuse about.

runners_data.name: Shrimp Shady
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's booking for this 4-year-old says everything — Shrimp Shady is in red-hot form (1-2-1-1-6 in recent starts) and comfortably handles Good to Firm, winning over 16f at Goodwood; a natural prominent racer who can slide into the ideal second-position slot behind Spirit Mixer and produce a telling late kick.

runners_data.name: Mountain Road
runners_data.note: Yutaka Take rides this Jim Goldie 7-year-old who has won twice over 16f on good and placed at 13f; 69 days since last run is a stamina question over 2m and the extra distance is a step beyond his proven best, but he travels prominently and could get a perfect low-pressure trip.

runners_data.name: Marnier
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore's 4-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by inclination — has won over 14f on good and placed in similar company — but sits in midfield on the map only because the field is loaded with rear-division types; connections will hope he finds his natural position but the congestion at the back makes that uncertain.

runners_data.name: Oneforthegutter
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' 7-year-old is another true hold-up operator whose recent form shows a string of seventh, eighth and fifteenth positions; pulled forward on the map by redistribution rather than by nature, and with a tongue-tie fitted, his chances hinge on finding a clear passage that his recent results suggest he struggles to exploit.

runners_data.name: Pole Star
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the mount on this Charlie Johnston 4-year-old who is a natural front-runner or prominent racer — yet the map places him in midfield because this field cannot accommodate all the aggressive types up front; if he cannot secure his preferred berth his STYLE_FIT discount is meaningful, and a run of 4-3-5-11-9 in recent starts does not inspire.

runners_data.name: Hermetic
runners_data.note: Christophe-Patrice Lemaire rides for Ian Williams, who saddles three in this race; Hermetic is a prominent type whose map position is midfield only by necessity — the horse has limited exposed form (three runs) and no experience beyond 16f on soft or standard, making this Good to Firm 2m trip a significant step into the unknown.

runners_data.name: Beylerbeyi
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR 101 and carrying 143lbs as a true hold-up horse, Beylerbeyi has been placed at Group level and has 2W2P from 15 runs on similar going; the weight burden is significant over 2m but Ian Williams' runner has the class to absorb it, and four runs in recent weeks suggest he is well-tuned.

races.paceDynamic: Spirit Mixer is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with only Kilmeaden and Shrimp Shady as natural prominent types to apply any pressure, she is likely to control this at a measured, sustainable gallop over the 2m trip on Good to Firm ground. That kind of uncontested lead at a steady tempo rewards the horse with most residual speed at the death, making late burst from midfield the crucial weapon. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the map can physically place — Pole Star and Hermetic are genuine prominent racers who are unlikely to secure that berth in a field this competitive, while Marnier and Oneforthegutter are true hold-up operators shuffled into a midfield slot on the map. This race shape most favours horses who can track the modest early pace in a handy position and produce a sustained gallop home — prominent-to-midfield types with proven form on Good to Firm over this sort of trip stand to benefit most.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Gallop, Finishers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Mixer dictates an uncontested, conservative pace through the first mile and the race only truly ignites over the final three furlongs.
scenarios.body: Spirit Mixer's solo lead at a sustainable tempo compresses the field and sets up a searching finish where those tracking closely in second or third row surge past in the straight; the long Ascot home straight amplifies the advantage of horses with a clean passage and a turn of foot.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Picks Up Early
scenarios.trigger: If Kilmeaden or Shrimp Shady push forward aggressively to test Spirit Mixer, turning this into a proper stamina examination.
scenarios.body: A genuinely contested early gallop stretches the field and drains the speed-reliant horses, leaving only the truest stayers standing at the 2f pole; horses with proven form at extreme distances and a willingness to grind come to the fore under those conditions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Hangs On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so moderate that a horse positioned just behind the leader steals first run down the straight and the chasers fail to close.
scenarios.body: A horse like Shrimp Shady, with strong recent form and the ability to quicken from a prime pitch just off the pace, kicks entering the straight before rivals can organise their challenges; the wide Ascot straight offers room to maintain momentum and hold on.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fast enough to string the field out and genuine hold-up horses get a clear late run to deliver a finishing burst.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Marnier, Oneforthegutter or Lavender Hill Mob to successfully close from a long way back — however, Marnier and Oneforthegutter are natural hold-up types displaced into midfield on the map and may not find their true position in the run, significantly reducing the likelihood of a perfectly executed late swoop; Lavender Hill Mob has the best credentials here given authentic hold-up credentials and a win over soft ground at 21f.

watchPoints.text: Shrimp Shady — Ryan Moore's booking on the in-form 4-year-old is the single biggest tactical pointer in this race; if he slots comfortably into second behind Spirit Mixer and travels strongly through the middle stages, he becomes the horse to beat in the straight.

Beylerbeyi's 143lbs weight — as the highest-rated horse in the field carrying top weight over a demanding 2m trip on Good to Firm, any sign of him labouring in the straight under that burden would shift the complexion of the race significantly toward the lighter-weighted finishers.

Pole Star and Hermetic at the start — both are natural prominent racers redistributed to midfield; watch whether either breaks smartly and muscles into a forward berth, as that would alter the pace equation and increase pressure on Spirit Mixer's lead.

Mountain Road — 69 days since last run for Jim Goldie's 7-year-old; if Yutaka Take finds him fresh and travelling sweetly through the first mile, the class of the Japan jockey could extract a big performance at a generous price, but the fitness flag is genuine.

Lavender Hill Mob — the only pure hold-up horse with a genuine win at this sort of extreme distance (21f on soft); if the pace quickens enough to stretch the field and Jamie Melham produces him widest of all in the straight, he is the one most likely to spring a late surprise from the rear group.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Challenge (Class 2 Handicap) (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Claymore
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who gets to lead uncontested here, which is exactly his preferred mode; Jerry Chau takes the ride and the 35-day break is unremarkable for a seven-year-old, but the STYLE_FIT tag reminds that if the race develops in a way that denies him the lead, his chance diminishes sharply — he is at his best when allowed to control.

runners_data.name: Insanity
runners_data.note: Alan King's six-year-old has consistent placed form including two recent second-place finishes at 10f-12f on Good, and Mme Marie Velon provides the Shergar Cup international jockey angle; a genuine hold-up horse who needs a genuine pace to pick up, and the controlled tempo here is a concern for his chance of landing this from the back.

runners_data.name: Frances Ethel
runners_data.note: William Haggas sends out this six-year-old for C Y Ho but the 248-day absence is a major flag — she has run only at 10f on Tapeta recently and her form on Good is limited to two moderate efforts; a hold-up type who needs everything to fall right and whose fitness query makes her difficult to trust at a competitive OR of 97.

runners_data.name: Night Breeze
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's six-year-old was last seen just 11 days ago finishing third and has strong recent 12f form on Good going with a win thrown in; a natural hold-up horse who travels well enough to be competitive if any pace develops, and the tight turnaround appears to suit given his last run was a close-up third.

runners_data.name: Enemy
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old carry-through from Ian Williams's yard with headgear (tp) applied and a very recent win over 16f on Standard, but his Good-ground form over this trip is poor — nine consecutive out-of-the-placings at this course and distance type; the style-fit is hold-up and the tempo must genuinely test the leaders for him to get into contention.

runners_data.name: Asgard's Captain
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's booking is the standout positive for Dylan Cunha's six-year-old, whose true racing style is hold-up but who has been pushed into a midfield map position by the weight of closers in this field; on the evidence of a recent fourth at 14f on Good, the trip suits, but the style displacement means he won't be racing from his most comfortable berth.

runners_data.name: Castle Stuart
runners_data.note: Richard & Fahey's four-year-old has solid recent form at 10f on Good (second and third), making the step up to 1m4f the key question; L J Ferraris rides, and while this horse's natural inclination is to come from off the pace, the crowded hold-up sector has shifted him into a midfield mapping — he may actually find that an easier berth than expected given his relative youth and his tendency to race handily.

runners_data.name: Sportingsilvermine
runners_data.note: James Owen's five-year-old won over 12f on Good last time and has two wins in the last five on similar ground, making him one of the more in-form horses here at the right trip; Yutaka Take's Shergar Cup ride is interesting, and as a prominent type he is naturally suited to sitting just behind Claymore and pressing from a good position throughout.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Believer
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's nine-year-old has been running frequently (15 days since last run) but his recent Good-ground form is limited — three runs in 15 on similar going with no wins; a true hold-up type mapped to midfield by the congested rear end, and Saffie Osborne will need to adapt tactics to suit a position that is not this horse's natural environment.

runners_data.name: Stem
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's four-year-old won at 10f on Good recently and was second at 8f, showing progressive form at a fair level; Jamie Melham rides for a yard in decent form (T14: 9/55), and as a prominent type Stem is one of the few horses here naturally suited to sitting close to Claymore and producing a sustained challenge once straightened.

runners_data.name: Genealogy
runners_data.note: Faye Bramley's four-year-old has placed twice at 16f on Good and won at that trip, so the step back to 1m4f is a slight shortening; no jockey listed is a minor flag for market watchers, and while this horse's genuine preference is to close from the rear, the overcrowded hold-up sector places it in midfield — the style displacement and the trip shortening combine to create uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Parlando
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's seven-year-old has placed at 10f on Good and won at that trip but has mixed form at 12f; a natural hold-up type repositioned into midfield by the field's composition, and at OR 86 — the lowest in the field — the weight pull over more exposed handicappers must work in its favour for a realistic winning chance.

races.paceDynamic: Claymore is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 1m4f handicap and, with no genuine pace rival likely to push him from the outset, he should be able to dictate a measured, controlled gallop around Ascot's straight track on Good to Firm ground. Sportingsilvermine and Stem are the prominent types most likely to sit just off him, but neither is a natural pace-maker so the tempo should remain sustainable rather than searching. The field is nominally packed with hold-up horses — Insanity, Night Breeze, Enemy, Asgard's Captain, Castle Stuart, Fantasy Believer, Genealogy, Parlando and Frances Ethel — but because there are far more hold-up types than the map can physically place at the rear, Castle Stuart, Asgard's Captain, Fantasy Believer, Genealogy and Parlando have been redistributed to midfield, meaning they will not be racing from their true natural position. A controlled pace with a strong-travelling leader and a compressed midfield strongly favours horses who can race prominently or sit just off the pace and produce a sustained gallop in the home straight, rather than those who depend on a strong pace to get into the race from well off it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Claymore Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Claymore sets a sustainable, uncontested pace and the hold-up horses fail to generate enough momentum from the rear.
scenarios.body: Claymore dictates from the front at a steady clip, and the horses tracking him closest — Sportingsilvermine and Stem — get the perfect gun-to-tape position to challenge over the final two furlongs; with no real pace injection from behind, those racing in the first four settle shortest to finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Claymore sets a stronger pace than expected and the field strings out, giving genuine closers a clear run.
scenarios.body: A genuinely honest gallop opens the race up so that horses ridden patiently — particularly those with recent solid form at this sort of trip — can pick off tired rivals inside the final furlong; Night Breeze, who has place form at 12f on Good and was most recently seen finishing third, and Insanity, consistent against similar marks, are best placed to benefit from this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed hold-up types adapt well to their unnatural midfield slot and produce a decisive late move.
scenarios.body: Horses such as Asgard's Captain and Castle Stuart, pushed forward by the congested field into midfield rather than their preferred back position, actually find themselves better placed than usual for this course and distance, delivering a sustained challenge from two furlongs out; this scenario requires them to overcome the style-fit discount, which limits its probability but keeps it firmly possible.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Two Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Stem or Sportingsilvermine press Claymore hard from the outset and kick clear as Claymore tires.
scenarios.body: Both prominent types accelerate away from a tiring front-runner in the straight, with the rest of the field having been set too much to do; this is the least likely shape because Claymore is expected to travel comfortably and the pace is unlikely to be searching enough to cause his collapse.

watchPoints.text: Claymore — if he gets a soft lead at a comfortable pace for the first mile, the race could be over a long way from home as no rival has the natural pace to bridge the gap if he quickens from the front.

Night Breeze — only 11 days since his last run and returned in a short turnaround, so connections clearly think he is in peak form; if Mme Marie Velon can get Insanity into a handy position early rather than buried at the back, a genuine late charge is on.

Ryan Moore on Asgard's Captain — Moore's booking in a Shergar Cup race carries tactical weight, and if he elects to position higher than this horse's natural hold-up style dictates, the redistribution into midfield could become a genuine advantage rather than a compromise.

Sportingsilvermine vs Stem — both prominent types will be competing for the same real estate directly behind Claymore; if they push each other for position in the early stages, the pace could lift unexpectedly and open the race up for the back-markers.

Frances Ethel — the 248-day absence from William Haggas's yard warrants monitoring in the market; if she shows strong support despite the layoff it suggests the stable is confident she returns fit, which would upgrade her hold-up threat significantly.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Sprint (Class 2 Handicap)

runners_data.name: Havana Hurricane
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid similar-going stats (10/11 runners beaten on Good), decent recent form over 6f at Ascot, Eve Johnson Houghton trainer; needs a genuine pace to close into and a clear passage — her best form is at 5f so the extra furlong is a minor query.

runners_data.name: Shaatir
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who wins this race's shape if he gets a clean break; Archie Watson sends him out fresh on 116 days off with a hood, and his best form is over this trip on Good — he simply needs to go unopposed, which the pace map strongly suggests he will.

runners_data.name: May Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up type by John & Thady Gosden with Lemaire aboard; best form has come at 7f and soft ground so the step back in trip and firmer surface are questions, though she showed up at 3rd on similar going twice — patient ride will be required.

runners_data.name: Red Spells Danger
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's consistent 3yo has won twice and placed five times over 6f on Good — one of the more likely prominent horses to actually secure a berth behind Shaatir in the early jostle; Saffie Osborne keeps the ride and the horse is in the form of its life on 14-day return.

runners_data.name: Figjam
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Katie Scott and C Y Ho whose form over 6f on Good shows limited wins; has been finishing mid-pack of late and may struggle if the prominent scrimmage goes against him — better over 7f in recent outings is a slight concern.

runners_data.name: American Gulf
runners_data.note: Genuinely long absence at 310 days for Oliver Cole's runner, whose best form came over 6f on Good (1W2P in last three attempts); prominent style and prior course form are positives but the layoff demands caution, and his last run was a blank.

runners_data.name: Jel Pepper
runners_data.note: Jel Pepper races with headgear and has solid Good-ground form, but has been finishing in mid-division recently and may be pushed back further than Stuart Williams would like; prominent at best, 39 days off is routine, but the 8f run suggests connections are searching for the horse's trip.

runners_data.name: Cape Ashizuri
runners_data.note: Dynamic hold-up horse for Dylan Browne McMonagle who won over this course and distance on Good last time; the 56-day break is not a concern given that preparation form, and a clear run suits his style enormously — one of the most naturally suited horses to this race shape.

runners_data.name: Thunder Call
runners_data.note: William Haggas has had a productive 14-day strike rate (10/52) and Thunder Call has won twice over 6f on similar surfaces; prominent racer who is among the most likely to secure a genuine front-rank berth, and his recent form string (113) suggests he is at peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Grasmere Boy
runners_data.note: In-form horse with back-to-back wins, but a natural prominent racer whose preferred position is likely to be squeezed out given the depth of pace in this field; Yutaka Take will need to adapt, and the style-fit discount (0.92) is a real consideration even if his raw form is strong.

runners_data.name: Anyasi
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's lightly-raced 3yo has won two of three on Good-ish ground and shapes like a genuine prominent type — but the congested race map means she will likely race further back than ideal; no jockey named adds an information gap, and the short form string makes her hard to fully assess.

runners_data.name: One And Gone
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's hold-up sprinter has been running over 5f and steps up here; back-to-back wins at 5f on Good are promising, but the 6f trip on this track is unproven and the hold-up style means he needs a true enough pace — he could be undone by an average gallop.

races.paceDynamic: Shaatir is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is set to stride clear from the gates and control tempo on Good to Firm ground at Ascot's straight 6f. Behind him, Red Spells Danger, Figjam, American Gulf, Jel Pepper, and Thunder Call all want prominent positions, creating a congested battle for the next handful of places between the 2f and 3f markers — that scramble risks scrubbing momentum from the prominent contingent mid-race. The hold-up horses Havana Hurricane, May Angel, Cape Ashizuri, and One And Gone will be last away or close to it, relying on a pace that is genuinely testing to close into. The field holds more prominent types than can physically slot in behind Shaatir, and it is Red Spells Danger and Thunder Call — both course-proven over this trip in this going — who are best placed to actually secure those berths; Grasmere Boy and Anyasi are true prominent racers who are most likely to find themselves shuffled further back than ideal. This race shape — a single uncontested leader setting a clear, measured pace — strongly favours hold-up horses who get a clean run in the final 2f, provided the moderate early gallop doesn't blunt their finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shaatir Leads, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Shaatir dictates a fair but not furious pace and the hold-up horses find daylight in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Shaatir rolls along in front with no pressure, setting a rhythm that keeps the field strung out enough for the closers to time their runs; horses like Cape Ashizuri and Havana Hurricane, who travel well off a strong gallop, get the soft lead they need before unleashing their finishes. Hold-up horses with proven form at 6f on Good to Firm are the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Squeeze Pays Off
scenarios.trigger: If the scrimmage for prominent positions resolves quickly and Red Spells Danger or Thunder Call slots in cleanly behind Shaatir without losing momentum.
scenarios.body: The pace congestion settles by the 4f pole and the two or three horses that secure the prime prominent berths get a tow into the race off Shaatir's tail, producing enough energy to sustain their challenge through the final furlong. Horses with the tactical pace to travel prominently and proven winning form at this trip on Good ground come out ahead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Shaatir Alone and Unpegged
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent traffic battle burns out the midfield and the hold-up horses get no clear run, leaving Shaatir's lead uncontested.
scenarios.body: Shaatir, fresh from a 116-day break, keeps rolling and the field behind him implodes — those who chased too hard fade, those who waited get blocked.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Chaos Late
scenarios.trigger: If a truly fast early pace develops from the prominent congestion, dramatically increasing the pace and setting up a late sprint for those furthest back.
scenarios.body: If the battling prominent types push the tempo harder than expected, the race fragments and one or two horses from the back group find a gap in the final furlong to mow down the field.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion: Red Spells Danger, Thunder Call, Figjam, American Gulf, and Jel Pepper all want the same early positions — watch for bumping or shuffling back between the 5f and 4f markers that could compromise multiple fancied runners.

Grasmere Boy and Anyasi are both natural prominent horses who are likely to find themselves further back than their trainers intend — if either gets caught in traffic two out, their genuine ability will be wasted by the race shape.

Shaatir returns from 116 days off with a hood and goes straight to the front — if the layoff shows in a stumbled break or a loss of jumping sharpness, the entire race dynamic changes and the prominent horses inherit control.

Cape Ashizuri was last seen finishing 19th before back-to-back wins — his form is extremely streaky and his hold-up style requires a clean split in the straight; watch whether McMonagle can find a gap as the finish approaches.

One And Gone steps up from 5f to 6f for the first time on this evidence — track how he travels in the first 2f, as a horse who has only won at 5f may find the extra ground exposes him on Good to Firm at Ascot.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Classic (Class 3 Handicap) (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Archers Bay
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back over 10f on Good ground with Ryan Moore in the plate; steps up to 1m4f here but the sire line suggests the extra furlong is fine — visor fitted (hg:p) and T14 form of 2/12 is modest, but Moore's presence and course experience make this a serious contender for the pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Hoseki
runners_data.note: William Haggas has an excellent T14 strike rate of 10/52 and this horse has won three of his last five on Good ground, all over 10-12f; sits just off the pace in a prominent role and Saffie Osborne is a sharp jockey for the Shergar Cup context — consistent form figure of 34-111 makes this one of the most straightforward profiles in the race.

runners_data.name: Baltic Fleet
runners_data.note: Has run vigorously in recent starts (hg:v) and Ian Williams has sent him out just 10 days ago — the blinkers may sharpen focus but the P placed run behind similar rivals at 12f on Good ground is the key form line; Jerry Chau inherits a prominent-running type who will need a clean run to convert his placed efforts.

runners_data.name: Blue Hercules
runners_data.note: Jamie Melham takes over a horse who has finished second twice in five starts, all on Good ground over 10-12f, without winning — the form is reliable but the profile screams consistent placer rather than winner, and his chance hinges on the pace burning off those ahead of him.

runners_data.name: Pierre Grosse
runners_data.note: L J Ferraris rides this John Harrington-trained hold-up type who has placed in seven of his last eight starts on Good or similar ground; the pattern of placing without winning is a slight concern, but the stamina and consistency over 10-13f on fast turf makes him the most natural beneficiary of a truly run race.

runners_data.name: Royal Poetry
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's charge has won over 12f on Good ground and carries a career form line showing strong placing ability — Yutaka Take is the headline Shergar Cup jockey angle here, and his tactical intelligence is a genuine asset if he can position Royal Poetry just behind the duelling leaders.

runners_data.name: King Of Berkshire
runners_data.note: Christophe-Patrice Lemaire takes on a horse who has won over 10f and 12f on Good ground and wants to lead — Andrew Balding's T14 rate of 10/53 is solid, but the key question is whether this horse can beat Archers Bay to the front and hold on over the extra furlong; the 1m4f trip is at the limit of his confirmed form.

runners_data.name: Level Look
runners_data.note: A hold-up type who was just 6 days ago on the track — the quick return for Andrew Balding suggests the stable think she is in good order; she won over 10f on Standard and has placed over 12f on Good ground, but the jockey, Mme Frida Valle Skar, is an amateur Shergar Cup rider which introduces tactical uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Ohara
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton sends out a horse whose form has been very mixed — a wide-margin win at 8f on Soft, then a string of mid-field finishes over longer trips on Good ground; the 14-day gap is fine but the 15th, 8th, and 9th-place finishes on Good over 12f suggest this trip and surface combination has not suited.

runners_data.name: Last Verse
runners_data.note: Joseph Parr's runner is a genuine hold-up horse by nature — his 1W over 12f on Good and three placed efforts show ability, but with the field stacked with prominent types ahead of him he will likely be shuffled further back than ideal; the redistribution into midfield on the map understates how far back he could end up, which tempers his chance in any shape that requires forward positioning.

runners_data.name: Tai Hang Pegasus
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes has this horse back out just 2 days after his last run, which is a very sharp turnaround and warrants monitoring for freshness — by nature a prominent runner with a win and three places over 12f on Good ground, but the compressed field means he is unlikely to secure his favoured tracking position, and racing from further back than usual reduces his effectiveness meaningfully.

races.paceDynamic: Archers Bay and King Of Berkshire are both confirmed front-runners who will compete for the lead from the gates over this 1m4f trip on Good to Firm ground, creating a genuinely contested early pace rather than a soft, uncontested gallop. With two horses fighting for the same rail position, the fractions are likely to be honest rather than dawdling, which stretches the field and sets up a searching examination of stamina in the straight. The field actually contains more prominent-running types than the race shape can absorb — Baltic Fleet, Blue Hercules, and Royal Poetry all want to race prominently, while Tai Hang Pegasus (a natural prominent type) and Last Verse (a true hold-up horse) have been pushed into positions they wouldn't naturally occupy, meaning the race will be even more compressed and competitive in the early-middle stages than the map suggests. With a genuine two-way pace battle up front and a field stacked with prominent runners, this race shape most strongly favours a horse who can sit just off the duelling leaders in a genuine rhythm and produce a sustained staying finish — the classic patient prominent-to-midfield profile over a mile and a half on fast ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Burns Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If Archers Bay and King Of Berkshire push each other through honest fractions and soften the field for a horse just off the pace to pounce.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set a genuine gallop that stretches the field and leaves them vulnerable late, handing the advantage to a horse tracking in third or fourth who has been travelling within itself. Hoseki, Royal Poetry, and Pierre Grosse all have the profile to capitalise, having shown the ability to sustain a finish over this trip from just off a strong pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Frontrunner Asserts Control
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace-setters — most likely Archers Bay — establishes early dominance and King Of Berkshire drops away, allowing a controlled, solo lead.
scenarios.body: A single front-runner dictating from the front at a measured but honest clip could prove very difficult to catch over 1m4f on Good to Firm ground, particularly if the field behind is fractious and bunched. Archers Bay, with Ryan Moore aboard and back-to-back wins over course-suitable trips, is the most likely beneficiary, with King Of Berkshire the alternative if he is the one to assert.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Staying Closers Sweep Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly fierce early and the entire prominent group cries enough in the final two furlongs, allowing genuine hold-up horses to sweep past.
scenarios.body: Pierre Grosse has the ideal hold-up profile and consistent form in similar conditions, while Level Look and Ohara have the ability to close from off the pace if the race fully falls apart at the front. Last Verse is technically a hold-up horse but has been mapped to midfield due to congestion, meaning this scenario's core hold-up pool is smaller than it appears and the probability is genuinely discounted.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops in a stop-start rhythm that suits a horse sitting mid-division who can explode off a slow final bend pace.
scenarios.body: Tai Hang Pegasus, though a natural prominent type pushed into midfield by the crowded pace, has the form to capitalise if the race falls perfectly — three placed efforts from the last four at this trip suggest fitness and consistency. Blue Hercules has repeatedly placed over 12f on Good ground but has yet to convert, and a muddled pace is his most likely route to a winner's enclosure.

watchPoints.text: Archers Bay and King Of Berkshire will battle for the lead from the start — watch for either one being pushed into an unsustainably fast early split that softens them both for Hoseki or Royal Poetry to pick up.
Tai Hang Pegasus has had only 2 days since his last run — watch for any signs of a stiff or flat performance early, as the turnaround is unusually sharp even for a fit horse.

Level Look is ridden by an amateur jockey in a competitive handicap — watch to see whether she gets a clean passage from the hold-up position, as any traffic trouble in a compressed field could end her race prematurely.

Pierre Grosse has finished placed in seven of his last eight starts without winning — watch whether Ferraris commits him earlier than usual to break the pattern, as a patient waiting ride has repeatedly left him just short.

Baltic Fleet's visor (hg:v) is fitted again after a P (pulled up) last time — watch his early behaviour and settling, as if he races freely against his nature in this contested gallop the visor could work against rather than for him.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Mile (Class 2 Handicap)

runners_data.name: Cerulean Bay
runners_data.note: Has led or pressed the pace in all recent starts and owns a consistent record at the mile on good ground with two runner-up finishes at this course — Jamie Melham should get a dream lead, though STYLE_FIT note tempers confidence about the quality of his win chance against a well-handicapped field.

runners_data.name: Two Tribes
runners_data.note: Roger Varian-trained runner whose recent form is at six and seven furlongs and who is stepping back up to a mile; his two best recent runs have come prominently, and the bit of headgear (blinkers) adds urgency — Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking is the standout jockey angle here.

runners_data.name: Crown Board
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator with a pair of placed efforts over a mile on good ground in recent history; Frida Valle Skar's international booking adds intrigue, and 14 days between runs is not a concern given Jane Chapple-Hyam's sharp strike rate over the fortnight.

runners_data.name: Mister Winston
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's four-year-old has won twice at the mile on good ground and sits prominently without forcing it — Jerry Chau is the jockey angle and Balding's strong recent trainer figures (10 from 53 in 14 days) make this a well-supported shape runner.

runners_data.name: Ebt's Guard
runners_data.note: Has placed in three of his last five starts at the mile on good ground and travels prominently; Suraj Narredu is an able booking and the horse is consistent without threatening to win, making him a solid each-way profile in the right scenario rather than a headline act.

runners_data.name: Fondo Blanco
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's four-year-old is 51 days fresh, wears a tongue tie, and his best form has come on soft or standard surfaces where his sim-going record is poor on turf — Good to Firm is a genuine concern, and Marie Velon's prominent ride will need to overcome that ground question.

runners_data.name: Bullet Point
runners_data.note: William Haggas's five-year-old is a natural front-runner or prominent racer who won at this trip on good ground, but an 84-day absence and the redistribution off his preferred position mean he must race less naturally today; Lemaire's class keeps him in calculations, though the combination of freshness and positional concession is a material discount.

runners_data.name: Popmaster
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who has placed at the trip before, but his sim-going record on fast ground is a concern (4 from 15), and Ed Walker's horse goes 35 days between runs as one of several genuine prominent types unable to get his natural slot — his claims rest on a scenario that is unlikely to fully materialise.

runners_data.name: Ozat
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's booking lifts Ozat above his recent form, which shows finishing eighth or lower in all five turf starts on good ground recently; a genuine hold-up horse, but his form record in this going band is thin and the single win was on soft, making the ground and flat form a twin concern.

runners_data.name: Serengeti
runners_data.note: Won over ten furlongs on good ground recently and is stepping back to a mile, which she has raced at before with mixed results; the trainer has zero winners from six in the past fortnight, and 50 days fresh is notable, though a hold-up style means she does not need to be forward early.

runners_data.name: Storm Star
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's five-year-old ran second over this course and trip on good ground, which is the key form line, but his sim-going record away from that context is poor and 51 days off adds a fitness caveat; as one of several prominent types displaced from his natural position, his chance is structurally discounted.

runners_data.name: Hickory
runners_data.note: Won over a mile on good ground in recent history and wears a hood, which has previously been associated with his better efforts; Jamie Osborne's eight-year-old is a natural prominent racer who cannot get that spot today, and the redistribution means he must produce his best while racing against type — a genuine class concern alongside the positional one.

races.paceDynamic: Cerulean Bay is the confirmed front-runner and, with no other genuine lead horse to challenge him, he will stride into a clear early position from the gates and control tempo on Good to Firm ground over Ascot's straight mile. The pack behind him features a cluster of natural prominent types — Bullet Point, Popmaster, Storm Star, and Hickory — but the map cannot accommodate all of them in their preferred positions, meaning several will be forced to race against their instincts in a more restrained, midfield role. Two Tribes, Mister Winston, Ebt's Guard, and Fondo Blanco represent the genuine second-tier prominent group who will track Cerulean Bay at a respectful distance, while Crown Board, Ozat, and Serengeti operate as true hold-up horses off the pace. On fast ground over a flat mile with a single unhurried pace-setter, this shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just behind Cerulean Bay and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out — a truly held-up closer will need an exceptional turn of foot late to bridge the gap that a controlled gallop creates. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions; Cerulean Bay takes the lead unchallenged, with Two Tribes and Mister Winston most likely to actually lock onto the prominent slots directly behind him.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cerulean Bay Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Cerulean Bay sets a measured, uncontested tempo and the race is decided by who tracks him most efficiently through the straight.
scenarios.body: Cerulean Bay dictates a comfortable pace from the front, and the horses sitting second or third early have every yard to build their effort without burning petrol — on fast Ascot ground this is the classic prominent-tracker's race shape. Mister Winston and Two Tribes, equipped to travel prominently and with sound records at the trip on similar going, are ideally positioned to challenge as the pace lifts inside the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front-Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Cerulean Bay's rivals all disengage and allow him a truly uncontested lead at a pace that never genuinely increases.
scenarios.body: With no pressure applied at any stage, Cerulean Bay can ration his effort and produce enough in the closing stages to hold on, particularly as the compressed finish suits a horse that has already saved vital energy mid-race. David O'Meara's horse has twice placed at this course and trip on similar ground, and Jamie Melham's ability to read a soft pace gives this scenario real teeth.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Held-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and the hold-up horses find a run through a compressed late-race pack.
scenarios.body: Crown Board has the most convincing form profile from off the pace at this trip on good ground, placing twice over a mile at similar tracks, and Serengeti's recent course win over ten furlongs shows she can sustain a late run when conditions suit. Ryan Moore on Ozat gives this scenario jockey-quality support, though Ozat's recent form has been moderate and the race shape must work perfectly for closers to pounce.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses mapped to midfield — Bullet Point, Popmaster, Storm Star, Hickory — manage to push forward and secure their natural position, quickening the pace significantly.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires several horses to simultaneously race against the map, creating a scramble for early position that lifts the tempo and burns out the front runners, leaving a mid-pack cover charge to land late. Bullet Point's single Ascot mile win and Hickory's recent placed record at the trip give them the best claims, but their redistribution tags mean this is the least reliable shape to back.

watchPoints.text: Cerulean Bay leads unchallenged — watch whether Two Tribes or Mister Winston track him closely enough from the outset, as any gap opened early on fast ground at Ascot could prove decisive by the time the straight stiffens.

Bullet Point is 84 days fresh and a natural prominent type mapped to midfield — if Lemaire pushes forward to reclaim his natural position in the early stages, it will quicken the pace significantly and change the entire shape of the race.

Fondo Blanco's ground record on Good to Firm or firm turf is weak (4 from 10 on sim going) — if the track rides quicker than the official description, his chance is materially reduced regardless of Roger Varian's overall form.

Ryan Moore on Ozat is the market-mover jockey angle to monitor — if Ozat drifts in the market it confirms the ground concern, but a significant move in would signal Moore has identified a tactical advantage in the hold-up position.

With four genuinely prominent horses redistributed to midfield positions (Bullet Point, Popmaster, Storm Star, Hickory), watch the first two furlongs for positional jostling — any early scrimmage for ground will artificially inflate the tempo and bring the hold-up horses Crown Board and Serengeti into contention late.
